item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is closer to the frozen contract because it leaves Files.Add and the global retry machinery unchanged and directly verifies retrying Upload from an *os.File. Both patches incorrectly duplicate Files.Add instead of routing through it, but A additionally makes a broad, explicitly forbidden behavioral change to every io.Reader request.","reasons":["B preserves the existing lower-level Files.Add behavior; A changes RawClient.Do to eagerly buffer arbitrary readers, altering Add, Update, and unrelated requests despite the contract forbidding retry-machinery refactoring.","B's retry test passes an opened file to Upload and confirms byte-identical multipart bodies across attempts, directly covering streamed-content retry. A's Upload retry test uses strings.Reader; its os.File test instead validates the out-of-scope Add behavior change.","Both Upload implementations duplicate Add's option forwarding, request execution, decoding, and missing-data handling rather than calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating the required single request path.","B's validation, multipart assertions, source-reader failure test, and replayability test provide strong coverage of the requested behavior."],"risks_a":["The global replayableReader change eagerly consumes and buffers all nonstandard io.Reader bodies whenever WithNoRetry is absent, even outside file uploads, creating compatibility and memory risks.","It explicitly changes Files.Add and Files.Update retry behavior, contrary to the requirement to preserve Add behavior and avoid unrelated retry refactoring.","Upload does not route through Files.Add, so the two implementations can drift in option, response, and error semantics."],"risks_b":["It explicitly violates scope by adding six association options and multipart-field machinery, despite the contract saying not to add association fields and to add exactly the Upload convenience API.","Upload calls NewFileWithFields rather than the required established NewFile helper.","Its new WithFile* options are misleadingly documented as applying to Add, but Add ignores cfg.form entirely and only Upload emits those fields; this is a confusing public API defect attributable to unnecessary scope expansion."]}
